rows.layout: Rows[tid][0..3] -> v4..v7 (only the first 32 of the 64 table rows: the wave32 run dispatches waveSize=32 threads)

notes: Test geometry for the wave32 run: one workgroup of 32 threads with waveSize*32 = 1024 dwords (4096 B) of LDS, which equals the oracle's fixed 4096 B group segment exactly. This matters: the ds_read/write_addtid_b32 cases deliberately use M0/offset combinations that land partly or wholly beyond 4 KiB (M0 0x7f000f9c + 36 + tid*4 crosses 0x1000; M0 0xff00 + offset 0xff00 is far out of range), so the expected values encode out-of-range LDS behaviour for a 4 KiB allocation. No rebasing is possible or wanted (M0 is set by s_mov in the body, offsets are immediates).

Plain ds_write_b32/ds_read_b32 use v80 = lane*4 (set in the body, word 5) plus offsets 0..3968: bytes 0..4095, all written by the fill loop before any read, so the uninitialised oracle LDS does not leak into results.
Body changes EXEC twice with s_and_saveexec_b32 s20 (lanes where input >> 30 != 0) and restores it itself with s_mov_b32 exec_lo, -1 (words 159, 181). M0 is left at -1, harmless.
36 asserted result columns (Checked = 36 of Results = 64; Check() compares all 36 against Expected32) in v10..v45: split into 3 adapters (columns 0-15, 16-31, 32-35).
Output columns 0..3 keep v6 (the third input) in lanes where the addtid read is masked off; words 136..139 initialise them inside the body.
verified: disassembly (llvm-mc gfx1030): prologue = v1/v3 address setup + buffer_load_dwordx4 v[4:7] offen; [5,247) = v80 = v0<<2, 32-plane ds_write_b32 fill, masked ds_read_addtid_b32 (4 M0 settings) into v10..v13, masked ds_write_addtid_b32 (4 M0 settings), 32 ds_read_b32 into v14..v45; stores v[10:45] at offsets 0..143. Run() (waveSize threads, waveSize*32 LDS dwords, userData = input/output descriptors only) and Check() (36 columns vs Expected32) read.
